setup.title: OmniRoute setup
setup.intro: OmniRoute is an open source gateway that runs on your computer. It gives your coding tools one local endpoint and routes their requests to the AI providers you connect. Follow these four steps on your computer.
needs: Node.js with npm, for the install command.

A free account with at least one provider. Some need an API key, approval or a payment method. [Check the free tiers guide](https://github.com/cheaper-inference/OmniRoute/blob/HEAD/docs/getting-started/FREE-TIERS-GUIDE.md).

sections.heading: Step 1: Install OmniRoute
sections.note: Let Claude do it, or run the command yourself.

steps.title: Copy the repo link
steps.body: Open the [OmniRoute repo](https://github.com/cheaper-inference/OmniRoute) and copy the link from the address bar.

steps.title: Ask Claude Code to install it
steps.body: Open Claude Code in your folder, paste the link and send this. Read what it plans to run before you approve it.

code.text: install this repo in my folder

steps.title: Or install it yourself
steps.body: This is the install from OmniRoute's own quick start. On npm 11 or later, npm may block the install scripts OmniRoute needs. If you see that warning, use the [allow-scripts command in the quick start](https://github.com/cheaper-inference/OmniRoute#-quick-start).

sections.heading: Step 2: Connect a free provider
sections.note: OmniRoute needs at least one connection before it can route anything.

steps.title: Choose one that fits
steps.body: Pick a provider whose current terms, privacy policy and quota work for you. Providers marked `tos: avoid` are left out of automatic routing by default.

steps.title: Connect it with your own account
steps.body: Add its API key or complete its account flow.

sections.heading: Step 3: Point Claude Code at OmniRoute

steps.title: Run configure
steps.body: It shows the models available to you and writes Claude Code's config.

steps.title: Pick auto
steps.body: Choose `auto` to route among your eligible connections, or pick one provider and model.

steps.title: Restart Claude Code
steps.body: Claude Code reads these settings once at startup, so close it and open it again.

sections.heading: Step 4: Check that it worked
sections.note: Your key is in the dashboard under Endpoints.

steps.title: List your models
steps.body: Replace `YOUR_KEY` with your OmniRoute key. You should get a list of models back.

steps.title: Launch it directly if you prefer
steps.body: This starts Claude Code against your local OmniRoute without writing a config.

tips.title: You are on a free model, not Claude.
tips.body: Answers, speed and limits depend on which provider handles the request.

tips.title: Keep client code out of it.
tips.body: Free tiers can log your requests or train on them. Read each provider's privacy policy before you send it anything private.

tips.title: The token number is an estimate.
tips.body: OmniRoute estimates about 1.6 billion free tokens a month across providers. You only get what the accounts you connect allow.

tips.title: Connect more than one provider.
tips.body: A fresh install can have no route available, and one free tier can run out. More connections give `auto` somewhere to go.

tips.title: Limits and terms still apply.
tips.body: OmniRoute does not change a provider's rules. Check them, because free tiers change.
